questions.text: Who proposed the first model of artificial neurons in 1943?
options: C) Warren McCulloch and Walter Pitts
questions.correct_answer: C) Warren McCulloch and Walter Pitts
questions.explanation: The module states: 'The year 1943: The first work which is now recognized as AI was done by Warren McCulloch and Walter Pitts in 1943. They proposed a model of artificial neurons.'

questions.text: What is the name of the test proposed by Alan Turing in 1950 to check a machine's ability to exhibit intelligent behavior?
questions.explanation: The module states: 'Alan Turing published "Computing Machinery and Intelligence" in which he proposed a test... called a Turing test.'

questions.text: Who coined the term 'Artificial Intelligence' and in what year?
questions.explanation: The module states: 'The year 1956: The word "Artificial Intelligence" first adopted by American Computer scientist John McCarthy at the Dartmouth Conference.'

questions.text: What was the name of the first artificial intelligence program created by Allen Newell and Herbert A. Simon in 1955?
questions.explanation: The module states: 'The year 1955: Allen Newell and Herbert A. Simon created the "first artificial intelligence program" which was named "Logic Theorist".'

questions.text: Who created the first chatbot named ELIZA in 1966?
questions.explanation: The module states: 'Joseph Weizenbaum created the first chatbot in 1966, which was named as ELIZA.'

questions.text: What is the term used to describe the period between 1974-1980 when there was a severe shortage of funding for AI research?
questions.explanation: The module states: 'AI winter refers to the time period where computer scientists dealt with a severe shortage of funding from the government for AI researches.'

questions.text: What technology brought AI back after the first AI winter in 1980?
questions.explanation: The module states: 'The year 1980: After AI winter duration, AI came back with "Expert System". Expert systems were programmed that emulate the decision-making ability of a human expert.'

questions.text: Why did the second AI winter occur between 1987-1993?
options: A) Because there were no researchers in AI.
B) Because of high cost but not efficient results from expert systems like XCON.
C) Because everyone lost interest in computers.
D) Because Deep Blue lost to Kasparov.
questions.correct_answer: B) Because of high cost but not efficient results from expert systems like XCON.
questions.explanation: The module states: 'Again, Investors and government stopped in funding for AI research due to high cost but not efficient results. The expert system such as XCON was very cost-effective.'

questions.text: In 1997, which AI system beat world chess champion Garry Kasparov?
questions.explanation: The module states: 'In the year 1997, IBM Deep Blue beat world chess champion, Gary Kasparov, and became the first computer to beat a world chess champion.'

questions.text: Which AI system won the quiz show Jeopardy in 2011 by understanding natural language and solving tricky questions?
questions.explanation: The module states: 'In the year 2011, IBM's Watson won Jeopardy, a quiz show, where it had to solve complex questions as well as riddles. Watson had proved that it could understand natural language and can solve tricky questions quickly.'
